title: Digital Reach Versus Real Loyalty: Measuring Mumbai Indians Beyond Followers
dek: Followers can be bought; loyalty is earned. The data cannot count Mumbai Indians' fans, but it can measure what they have been given to stay loyal to.
excerpt: Mumbai Indians have won at least half their matches in a measurable number of seasons, with a longest playoff drought the data can pin down. Those are the conditions loyalty has had to survive.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: Reach Is Not Loyalty
body: Follower counts measure reach: how many people could see a post. Loyalty is different: whether people stay, return and spend when results turn.
The CricField warehouse is ball-by-ball cricket data. It contains no follower, engagement, membership or ticket-renewal data, so it cannot measure the commercial side of this question directly.

sections.heading: What Fans Have Been Given
body: What the data can measure is the experience fans have been loyal to. Mumbai Indians have won at least half their decided matches in {{ev:dr-above}} of {{ev:dr-n-seasons}} seasons and reached the playoffs in {{ev:dr-playoffs}}.
Their season win rates have a spread of {{ev:dr-sd}} percentage points, and their longest run without a playoff place is {{ev:dr-drought}} seasons.

sections.heading: Measuring Loyalty Properly
body: Real loyalty measures include repeat ticket buyers, membership renewals, attendance in losing seasons and engagement that persists after defeats.

sections.heading: Why Consistency Matters
body: A franchise with steady results asks less of its fans than one that swings between highs and lows. The spread of season win rates is a simple measure of that swing.
Whether steadiness or occasional glory builds deeper loyalty is a question for fan data, not match data.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Measure Retention, Not Reach
body: Mumbai Indians should judge their fan base on retention through bad seasons rather than follower totals.
The season record here is the context any such measure has to be read against.
